## Research {.section-title}
<hr class="section-rule">

We take a **comparative approach** to understanding human uniqueness, combining biological anthropology, palaeontology, and evolutionary biology to investigate how and why humans and other primates came to look and behave as they do today. Our work draws on a broad methodological toolkit:

```{=html}
<div class="row g-4 mt-3">

  <div class="col-md-6 col-lg-4">
    <div class="research-card">
      <div class="rc-icon">🦴</div>
      <h4>3D Morphometrics & Shape Analysis</h4>
      <p>We use geometric morphometrics and 3D scanning to quantify anatomical variation across 
      primates and hominins, identifying patterns of shape change through evolutionary time and 
      testing hypotheses about adaptation and constraint.</p>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="col-md-6 col-lg-4">
    <div class="research-card">
      <div class="rc-icon">⚙️</div>
      <h4>Virtual Computational Biomechanics</h4>
      <p>We use computational modelling to reconstruct and investigate the biomechanical performance of biological structures and systems in living and extinct species. Combining approaches such as finite element analysis, computational fluid dynamics, and musculoskeletal modelling, we explore locomotion, feeding, tool use, and other functional adaptations throughout human and primate evolution.</p>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="col-md-6 col-lg-4">
    <div class="research-card">
      <div class="rc-icon">🌳</div>
      <h4>Phylogenetic Comparative Methods</h4>
      <p>We develop and apply statistical methods for analysing trait evolution along phylogenetic 
      trees — estimating divergence times, modelling rates of morphological and life-history 
      change, and testing macroevolutionary hypotheses across primates and hominins.</p>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="col-md-6 col-lg-4">
    <div class="research-card">
      <div class="rc-icon">🧠</div>
      <h4>Human Brain & Body Evolution</h4>
      <p>A major focus is on the evolution of encephalization and body size in the hominin lineage — 
      including the timing, tempo, and drivers of brain expansion, and what distinguishes 
      <em>Homo sapiens</em> from earlier hominins and our primate relatives.</p>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="col-md-6 col-lg-4">
    <div class="research-card">
      <div class="rc-icon">🦧</div>
      <h4>Primate Adaptive Evolution</h4>
      <p>We investigate the adaptive radiation of primates — how they diversified into different 
      ecological niches, how their locomotor and dietary anatomy evolved, and what drives 
      macroevolutionary patterns of diversification and body plan innovation.</p>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="col-md-6 col-lg-4">
    <div class="research-card">
      <div class="rc-icon">🌍</div>
      <h4>Palaeoanthropological Fieldwork</h4>
      <p>We participate in the 
      <a href="https://www.gorongosa.org/science/palaeo-primate-project" target="_blank">Palaeo-Primate Project</a> 
      in Gorongosa National Park, Mozambique, recovering Miocene fossil primates from 
      the southern East African Rift — some of the oldest known from coastal woodland environments.</p>
    </div>
  </div>

</div>
```
